subject: English
topic: Reading Comprehension — Artificial Intelligence & Labour Market (W13 B1)

questions.stem: Passage: 'Artificial intelligence is reshaping the labour market in ways both dramatic and subtle. Unlike previous waves of automation — which primarily displaced manual and clerical workers — AI has the capacity to perform complex cognitive tasks: analysing legal documents, diagnosing medical conditions, generating creative content and writing computer code. This has led some economists to predict that no profession is truly safe from technological disruption. Others, however, argue that AI will primarily augment human capabilities rather than replace workers entirely, creating new categories of employment we cannot yet imagine.' — Which statement BEST reflects the passage's view on AI's impact?

options.option_text: AI will cause mass unemployment by eliminating all jobs.
AI affects only manual and clerical workers, not professionals.
Economists are divided on whether AI replaces or augments human workers.
AI is a less disruptive force than previous waves of automation.

questions.explanation: C is correct. The passage presents TWO views: some economists predict no profession is safe (replacement threat), while OTHERS argue AI augments human capability and creates new jobs. C accurately captures this division. Trap: A = overstates by saying 'all jobs' (passage says no profession is 'truly safe', not eliminated); B = directly contradicts the passage (AI performs cognitive tasks beyond clerical work); D = passage says AI differs FROM previous automation by targeting cognitive tasks (implies it is potentially more disruptive, not less).

questions.stem: [Same passage] The word 'AUGMENT' as used in the passage most closely means:

options.option_text: replace completely
suppress or limit
enhance or add to
copy or imitate

questions.explanation: C is correct. AUGMENT = to make greater by adding to; to enhance or supplement. 'AI will augment human capabilities' = AI will ADD TO and ENHANCE what humans can do, not replace them. Root: Latin augere = to increase. Trap: 'replace' = the passage contrasts augmenting with replacing; 'suppress' = opposite of augment; 'copy' = mimic (different concept — augmenting means improving, not imitating).

questions.stem: [Same passage] According to the passage, how does AI-driven automation DIFFER from previous waves of automation?

options.option_text: Previous automation was faster and more efficient.
Previous automation displaced manual workers; AI targets cognitive tasks too.
AI only affects developing countries, unlike earlier automation.
Previous automation created more new jobs than AI is expected to.

questions.explanation: B is correct. The passage explicitly states: 'Unlike previous waves of automation — which primarily displaced manual and clerical workers — AI has the capacity to perform complex cognitive tasks.' B captures this contrast precisely. Trap: A = no comparison of speed is made; C = no geographic distinction is mentioned; D = the passage presents both views on job creation without comparing them to previous automation's job creation.

questions.stem: [Same passage] The phrase 'categories of employment we cannot yet imagine' suggests the author believes:

options.option_text: Future jobs will be very similar to current ones.
AI will create jobs that are entirely new and unprecedented.
It is impossible for humans to predict economic trends.
AI development should be slowed to protect existing jobs.

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Categories of employment we cannot yet imagine' = types of jobs that do not currently exist and are so novel that present-day thinkers cannot predict them. This suggests AI may create fundamentally new work categories. Trap: A = 'cannot yet imagine' means UNLIKE current jobs (opposite); C = the passage doesn't say economic prediction is impossible in general — only that future AI-created jobs are unpredictable; D = the author is not making a policy recommendation (just presenting the optimists' view).

questions.stem: [Same passage] The tone of the passage can best be described as:

options.option_text: Alarmist and pessimistic
Dismissive of AI's economic impact
Balanced and analytical
Enthusiastically pro-AI

questions.explanation: C is correct. The author presents both alarm (no profession truly safe) and optimism (AI creates new jobs) without personally endorsing either view. This balanced presentation is analytical and academic in tone. Trap: alarmist = one-sided fear (passage also presents the optimistic view); dismissive = the opposite (passage takes AI's impact very seriously); enthusiastically pro-AI = passage acknowledges disruption concerns too.

questions.stem: Passage 2: 'The Indian education system has long been criticised for its emphasis on rote memorisation over critical thinking. While this approach may produce students who perform well in standardised examinations, it often fails to develop the problem-solving and communication skills that employers now demand. Education reformers increasingly advocate a shift towards competency-based learning — measuring students not by their ability to recall facts but by their demonstrated capacity to apply knowledge creatively and independently.' — What is the MAIN critique of rote memorisation raised in the passage?

options.option_text: It prevents students from performing well in examinations.
It prioritises exam performance over skills valued in the workforce.
It is practised only in India and not in other countries.
It was once effective but is now entirely obsolete.

questions.explanation: B is correct. The passage says rote learning 'produces students who perform well in standardised examinations' but 'fails to develop the problem-solving and communication skills that employers now demand.' The main critique = exam success but workforce skill deficiency. Trap: A = the passage says rote learning DOES help in exams (opposite); C = no comparison to other countries is made; D = 'once effective but now obsolete' overstates — the passage says it produces exam performers but lacks other skills.

questions.stem: [Same passage 2] What does 'COMPETENCY-BASED LEARNING' prioritise according to the passage?

options.option_text: Recalling factual information quickly under pressure
Demonstrated ability to apply knowledge creatively and independently
Covering a wide syllabus across many subjects
Competitive examination performance at national level

questions.explanation: B is correct. The passage defines competency-based learning as 'measuring students not by their ability to recall facts but by their demonstrated capacity to apply knowledge creatively and independently.' B is a direct paraphrase. Trap: A = recalling facts is what ROTE learning emphasises (the system being replaced); C and D = broad syllabus coverage and national exams are also associated with the old system, not competency-based reform.

questions.stem: [Same passage 2] The word 'ADVOCATE' as used in 'Education reformers increasingly advocate a shift' most closely means:

options.option_text: oppose or resist
publicly recommend or support
study or analyse in depth
implement or carry out

questions.explanation: B is correct. ADVOCATE (verb) = to publicly recommend or support a policy or cause. 'Education reformers increasingly advocate a shift' = they are recommending/promoting a change. Note: advocate (noun) = a lawyer or supporter. Trap: 'oppose' = the opposite; 'implement' = to actually carry out (advocacy is recommending, not necessarily implementing); 'study' = research (advocates act, they don't just study).

questions.stem: [Same passage 2] The passage implies that employers value which of the following MOST?

options.option_text: Scores achieved in national-level examinations
The ability to memorise and reproduce information accurately
Problem-solving and communication abilities
The breadth of subjects studied in school

questions.explanation: C is correct. The passage states rote learning 'fails to develop the problem-solving and communication skills that EMPLOYERS NOW DEMAND.' Employers therefore value problem-solving and communication. Trap: exam scores and memorisation = what rote learning produces (which employers are said NOT to demand); breadth of subjects = traditional curriculum (not highlighted as what employers value).

questions.stem: [Same passage 2] Which sentence would BEST continue the passage after its final sentence?

options.option_text: However, rote memorisation remains the only effective teaching method.
Such reforms would require retraining teachers and redesigning assessments across the system.
India's examination boards should stop conducting national tests altogether.
Students who memorise well inevitably become successful professionals.

questions.explanation: B is correct. The passage ends with advocacy for competency-based learning. The LOGICAL next step in such an argument is to address what IMPLEMENTING this reform would require — teacher retraining and redesigned assessments. This advances the argument naturally. Trap: A = contradicts the entire thrust of the passage (which criticises rote learning); C = extreme policy recommendation beyond the scope of what the passage advocates; D = directly contradicts the critique of rote learning made throughout the passage.
